newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks end higher on retail trading.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks end higher on retail trading.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks ended slightly higher on Monday led mostly by increased retail trade, brokers said.
They said the market was witnessing an unpaward trend, which was likely to continue as second half corporate results were expected to be better.
The Colombo all share index ended 8.6 point higher at 796.
"There was buying pressure in the morning, but it eased off slightly after sellers began getting into the market," said Alistair Corera of Forbes & Walker stock brokers.
"Retail trade dominated the market and trading was not in large quantities. Prices moved up on popular stocks like John Keells and Sampath Bank," said Ralph Wijesinghe of Asia Capital.
Foreign funds were barely active in the market on Monday, after they bought heavily in the last week.
Turnover was down shraply to 74 million rupees against more than 330 million on Thursday, the last trading day.
Colombo Dockyard was up three rupees at 25.5, Lanka Orix rose sharply by 15 rupees to 245, Sampath Bank was up three rupees to 76.
